attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to provide NAT egress for node2 and node3 on a private /24 (10.60.60.0/24 over eth1), implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the pre-provisioned control node). node1 got a static LAN address (10.60.60.254/24 on eth1) plus a VyOS source-NAT masquerade rule (10.60.60.0/24 -> eth0). node2/node3 got a new NetworkManager eth1 profile (10.60.60.11/.12) with a lower-metric default route via node1, so their default internet path now genuinely transits node1's NAT. Verified via api.ipify.org and live NAT translation tables. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node2, node3, node1, node4), confirming a changed boot_id and full recovery of NAT config, network profiles, and Ansible tooling after each restart, plus a clean idempotent playbook re-run at the end.
